Author: Krull RE, Chen P, Novak J, Kirk M, Barnes S, Baker J, Krishna NR, Caufield PW.##Chikindas ML, Nov?k J, Driessen AJ, Konings WN, Schilling KM, Caufield PW.##Nicolas G, Morency H, LaPointe G, Lavoie MC.##Nov?k J, Caufield PW, Miller EJ.
Comments:
Function: Mutacin-2 inhibits other mutans streptococci as well as many gram-positive exogenous pathogens. Transiently and partially depolarizes the transmembrane electrical potential and pH gradient of susceptible cells, inhibits the uptake of amino acids and depletes the intracellular ATP pool.
Biophysicochemical properties: pH dependence (Stable from pH 4.0 to 10.0); Temperature dependence (Thermostable).
PTM: There are one didehydrobutyrine (T25), two lanthionines (S12-C26; S19-C27) and one Beta-methyllanthionine (T10-C15).
Hemolytic_activity: No hemolysis information or data found in the reference(s) presented in this entry
Name: Mutacin-2 (Mutacin II mutacin H-29B; Bacteriocin)
Reference: J Biol Chem. 2000 May 26;275(21):15845-15850.##Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 1995 Dec;39(12):2656-2660.##BMC Microbiol. 2006 Apr 20;6:36.##J Bacteriol. 1994 Jul;176(14):4316-4320.
Target_Organism: Gram-positive bacteria: Micrococcus luteus, Staphylococcus aureus, Peptostreptococcus micros, Pediococcus acidilactici, Clostridium sporogenes, Corynebacterium diphtheriae, Actinomyces viscosus, Gardnerella vaginalis, Propionibacterium acnes, Listeria monocytogenes, Mycobacterium smegmatis.##Gram-negative bacteria: Campylobacter jejuni, Helicobacter pylori, Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
Title: Biochemical structural analysis of the lantibiotic mutacin II.##Mutacin II, a bactericidal antibiotic from Streptococcus mutans.##Mutacin H-29B is identical to mutacin II (J-T8).##Isolation and biochemical characterization of a novel lantibiotic mutacin from Streptococcus mutans.
